text: It was at Weatherend, a great house full of pictures and treasures, that John Marcher, after many years, found himself face to face again with May Bartram, a woman whose face he half remembered. <break time="0.8s" /> He had the odd impression that their earlier meeting had mattered more than he could recall, and that she, unlike himself, had kept every detail of it alive through all the intervening years. <break time="0.8s" /> He began by recalling that they had met in Rome some eight years before, but she corrected him gently, saying that it had been at Naples, and nearer ten years than eight. <break time="0.8s" /> Then, with a quiet smile, she reminded him of something he had entirely forgotten, namely that during one of those Italian afternoons he had confided to her a strange and deeply private secret. <break time="0.8s" /> He had told her that he had always felt, deep within himself, that something rare and strange, possibly prodigious and terrible, was waiting for him and would sooner or later happen. <break time="0.8s" /> Hearing that she had kept his secret for ten years without sharing it with anyone, Marcher felt, for the first time in his life, that he was no longer entirely alone with it. <break time="0.8s" /> Has it ever happened, she asked, and when he answered that it had not, she listened without a trace of mockery, and soon they agreed to watch for it together.
